articles.title: Trump replaces Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff
articles.summary: Democrats continue to celebrate one of the most lopsided midterm election victories in modern U.S. history, routing their Republican rivals to gain control of the U.S. House, U.S. Senate and statehouses across the country. In the Senate, Democrats flipped seven seats and now hold 54 to the Republican Party's 44. Two seats — nail-biting contests in Alaska and Mississippi — remain undeclared. In the House, Democrats held 253 House seats to the GOP's 161 as of 2 p.m. ET Friday, comfortably passing the majority threshold of 218, with 21 races yet to be called. The latest estimates show that the party is on track to win its largest majority since 2008. And there are still seats it could flip, including Colorado's Fourth District, which is held by Republican incumbent Rep. Lauren Boebert, a staunch Trump ally, whose race against Democrat Eileen Laubacher remains tight. There were also gubernatorial races , mayoral contests, ballot measures — and plenty of firsts. Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms of Georgia became the first Black woman elected governor in U.S. history, while Democrat Amy Acton became the first woman elected governor of Ohio. In Florida, Republican Byron Donalds became the state's first Black governor-elect. El-Sayed will be America's first Muslim senator. In a big post-election shake-up, President Trump on Friday announced that Stephen Miller, a top deputy widely viewed as one of the most influential figures behind the administration's agenda, is replacing Susie Wiles as his chief of staff. Earlier this week, Trump signaled he would work with Democrats during his remaining two years in office but said he wouldn't hesitate to use his veto power. Trump also acknowledged that the Iran war contributed to Republican losses, but defended his decision to pursue the conflict. "If I had to do it again, I'd have to do it again," he said, adding: "You can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon." Vice President JD Vance, though, blamed the scale of GOP losses squarely on the war with Iran. "The real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone," he wrote in a post on X . "The reason we lost is the war." articles.title: Sen. Chris Murphy is released from hospital after hemorrhagic stroke
articles.summary: Washington — Democratic Sen. Chris Murphy of Connecticut was released from the hospital Friday after experiencing a stroke nearly a week ago, but will miss several weeks of votes as he continues his recovery at a rehabilitation center. "I want to be direct with you, so here is my diagnosis," Murphy said in a statement. "Last Saturday afternoon, I felt something was not right with my body and called 9-1-1 out of an abundance of caution, and I'm glad I did." Murphy, who is 53, said he was diagnosed with a small bleed in the thalamus region of his brain. The thalamus sits above the brainstem and relays sensory information between the spinal cord and the brain, according to the Cleveland Clinic . Dr. Jose Suarez, the chief of neurosciences critical care at Johns Hopkins, where Murphy was hospitalized, said the senator experienced a small hemorrhagic stroke. "He has shown tremendous progress, and at the current rate of improvement, we expect that he will make a full recovery following rehabilitation," Suarez said in a statement released by Murphy's office. Murphy said he is taking his recovery seriously and will be spending several weeks at a rehabilitation center in order to "get back to work on the quickest timeline possible." "This has been a scary experience for me and my family, and I appreciate the continued respect for our privacy," Murphy said. "As I'm working towards a full recovery, I am staying engaged with my team and colleagues remotely, and my staff continues to carry out our legislative priorities, serve constituents, and ensure the work of my office continues uninterrupted." Murphy's office announced Sunday that he had numbness in his arm while at his son's hockey game and was taken to a local hospital, where it was discovered that he had a stroke. He was then transferred to Johns Hopkins. The senator has been viewed as a possible contender for the White House in 2028. articles.title: 2 DOJ officials resign, including attorney who oversaw 'grand conspiracy' probe
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — The top federal prosecutor in Miami who had been tasked with overseeing an investigation into foes of President Donald Trump has resigned, joining other high-profile Justice Department officials departing in the wake of the midterm elections, officials said Friday. Jason Reding Quiñones' resignation follows frustrations among Washington officials with his management of the office assigned to lead the so-called "grand conspiracy" investigation, according to people familiar with the matter who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss personnel issues. The Justice Department's top national security official, John Eisenberg, also resigned on Friday, Attorney General Todd Blanche said. On Thursday, Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon, who led a radical overhaul of the department's Civil Rights Division , also announced her departure. Quiñones was confirmed by the Senate last year as U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Florida, where the Justice Department had centered its meandering probe into whether former law enforcement and intelligence officials conspired against the Republican president. His departure comes as the investigation has shown signs of faltering amid a spate of staff turnovers and delays. Investigators in recent weeks have put off scheduled grand jury testimony of several witnesses, according to multiple people familiar with the matter who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss an ongoing investigation. Blanche said in a social media post that the department is grateful for Quiñones' "leadership in combating violent crime, drug trafficking, sex trafficking, and transnational crime, including the indictment of Raúl Castro." Castro, the former Cuban president, was indicted by Quiñones' office in May on charges related to the 1996 downing of civilian planes flown by Miami-based exiles. Quiñones said Friday that he is leaving with "immense pride in what we accomplished together and profound gratitude for the opportunity to serve our great Nation." "I am grateful to President Trump for his trust and to the extraordinary men and women of the great Southern District of Florida for their dedication, friendship, and unwavering commitment to justice and the rule of law," Quiñones wrote in a social media post. The "grand conspiracy" investigation has proceeded in fits and starts for over a year with repeated setbacks and departures. Last April, a lead national security prosecutor in the investigation of former CIA Director John Brennan was replaced on the team after raising questions about the strength of the case. Shortly afterward, Joseph diGenova, a former U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, took over the probe. DiGenova resigned from the Justice Department in September without bringing any criminal charges. Eisenberg was sworn in as assistant attorney general in charge of the department's National Security Division in June 2025 and oversaw cases involving espionage, terrorism, export control violations, cyber crimes and other matters. Among the division's most high-profile cases under his watch was the prosecution of former national security adviser John Bolton, who pleaded guilty this year to allegations of mishandling classified information and is awaiting sentencing. "He has served with distinction, strengthening our nation's ability to address threats, both foreign and domestic," Blanche said in a statement. articles.summary: In the early hours of Dec. 26, 1996, after a festive family Christmas, Patsy Ramsey walked down the stairs in her Boulder, Colorado, home to discover a terrifying ransom note telling her that her 6-year-old daughter JonBenét Ramsey had been kidnapped. She immediately called 911 and the Boulder Police Department responded to the scene in three minutes. Courtesy of John Andrew Ramsey - PHOTO: JonBenét Ramsey was 6 years old when she was found dead in her home in Boulder, Co. on Dec. 26, 1996. The taunting two-and-a-half-page ransom note was addressed to JonBenét's father, John Ramsey, and demanded $118,000 for the safe return of his daughter. "You stand a 99% chance of killing your daughter if you try to out smart [sic] us," the letter said. There was no sign of JonBenét or further communication from the would-be kidnappers. Hours later, a police officer asked John Ramsey and a friend to look through the house to see if anything seemed out of place. John Ramsey discovered his daughter’s lifeless body in the basement of their home. DNA testing confirms 'serial killer' in Pennsylvania in 1970s: State police An autopsy report determined that JonBenét had been sexually assaulted and killed by blunt force trauma to the head and strangulation, which was carried out with a makeshift corded torture device called a garrote. With 19 new interviews, ABC News anchor Diane Sawyer and chief investigative correspondent Aaron Katersky take a fresh look at this cold case, talking with investigators, forensic scientists, genealogy experts, the Boulder Police chief and JonBenét's brothers Burke Ramsey and John Andrew Ramsey, among others. Courtesy of John Andrew Ramsey - PHOTO: JonBenét Ramsey with her mother, Patsy Ramsey, both of whom competed in pageants. In the weeks and months after the murder, members of the Ramsey family came under intense scrutiny by both the Boulder police and the general public. Skeptics of the family pointed to several details of the case, including the ransom note, which some close to the investigation believed was staged by a family member to cover up JonBenét's death. The note was written on Patsy Ramsey’s notepad but after numerous handwriting comparisons, only one indicated that the samples showed any similarities to Patsy’s writing. The Ramsey family vehemently denied any claims they were involved in their daughter's death. In 2008, DNA was detected on the outside of JonBenét's pajama bottoms using a new testing method called touch DNA analysis. It matched the DNA found inside JonBenét's underwear and traced to the same unknown male, and not to any member of the Ramsey family. In recent years, a new technology called single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) has made it possible to solve cold murder cases nationwide . The advanced testing can retrieve DNA from miniscule samples. Combined with genetic genealogy, it allows officials to identify suspects by matching DNA to that of distant family members in law enforcement databases, using online genetic databases. articles.title: Polar vortex could bring an early blast of winter to the eastern U.S.
articles.summary: The polar vortex is weakening unusually early, forecasters have said, with a rare disruption possible within days that could send Arctic air traveling south over North America. The polar vortex is a band of powerful winds in the stratosphere that circle the North Pole each winter. It keeps the coldest air locked high in the atmosphere until it is disrupted. Once the vortex weakens, pockets of that air can be pushed south, which can bring frostier temperatures to parts of the U.S. In its updated November outlook, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's (NOAA) Climate Prediction Center said a disruption of the polar vortex could occur within days, possibly developing into a sudden stratospheric warming, which it called "very rare" for November. It warned that if this happens, its effects could last up to two months. The polar vortex made its mark this January, when a lobe of Arctic air pushed south, bringing a deep freeze to the eastern U.S. and Canada. Parts of northern Minnesota fell to -43°F on Jan. 24, according to state climate data , with states like Indiana also experiencing record lows as Greenland's west coast recorded its warmest January on record . NOAA said any effects in the eastern U.S. could compete with the influence of El Niño, which is still steering its outlook toward a milder November for much of the country. Here's what we know so far — and what that could mean for your weather. What does it mean for the weather? While strong sudden stratospheric warmings can disrupt the vortex and start the chain of events that sends the blasts of cold air down to North America, the jury is still out on whether the latest disruption will do this. This NOAA graphic shows what happens when the polar vortex weakens. NOAA At NOAA's winter outlook briefing on Oct. 15, Jon Gottschalck, a branch chief at the Climate Prediction Center, said the combination of a strong El Niño and a westerly wind pattern high in the tropical atmosphere typically favors a stronger, more stable polar vortex, and in turn, fewer Arctic air outbreaks. He added that cold outbreaks should still be expected at times, but with more warmer-than-normal days overall. If it takes hold, NOAA said the eastern U.S. is where effects could be felt, but El Niño's influence could compete against that. The climate phenomenon, which is currently in full swing and is expected to stay strong through at least late winter, warms the Pacific Ocean and generally brings milder weather to the U.S. There is a high chance it will become the strongest since records began in 1950. NOAA said that as the polar vortex approaches, it's worth getting prepared. "There is no cause to be alarmed when you hear about the polar vortex, but you should be prepared for colder temperatures," its guidance said. "Check the forecast for your area on weather.gov to ensure you are dressed appropriately. It is also a good idea to check the items in your home and car emergency kits at the beginning of each winter season to ensure you are prepared for any type of hazardous winter weather," the agency added. Why is the polar vortex weakening so early? The polar vortex normally strengthens through the fall as the Arctic cools, creating a whirlpool of air above the North Pole, which is why a breakdown in November would be so unusual. The vortex weakens in summer and strengthens in winter, with the winds forming miles above the North Pole. It holds its position in the Arctic until around December or January. It can be disrupted when big swells of air from lower in the atmosphere bump into it from below, making it wobble and slow down. The big disruptions, known as a "sudden stratospheric warming," usually occur in deep winter, and can stretch or split the vortex, displacing the cold air and sending it further south. If a major warming occurs within the coming days, it could be one of the earliest disruptions on record, experts told the Scientific American . The earliest polar vortex weakening previously recorded was Nov. 28, 1968. "As a weather fan, this is a big event because it's so unprecedented," Judah Cohen, a climatologist at Massachusetts Institute of Technology told the publication. articles.title: Meghan Markle's father Thomas arrested on charges related to child sexual abuse material
articles.summary: Meghan Markle's estranged father, Thomas Markle, was arrested in Florida on Friday on charges related to child sexual abuse material, authorities said. Markle, 82, was arrested by the FBI at a care home near Tampa, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of California said in a press release . He was charged with one count of possession of child pornography. Authorities said Markle was arrested after agents discovered approximately 78 items — including slides, film negatives, and books — that contained suspected child sexual abuse material (CSAM) while searching two storage units registered to Markle, at least one of which was in the Los Angeles area. "Mr. Markle is accused of possessing child sexual abuse material, including photographs depicting himself with minor girls," First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli said. "These allegations are extremely serious, and we will prosecute Mr. Markle to the fullest extent of federal law." The statement said that, in October 2026, law enforcement learned that an individual signed an affidavit regarding the discovery of suspected CSAM among Markle's possessions in the Philippines. Officers then interviewed a separate individual who revealed Markle had rented a storage unit in the Los Angeles area. This led to the discovery of a second storage unit. Both had been rented by Markle since 2008. FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement that “Markle allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions.” “This FBI will use every single resource at our disposal to protect innocent kids – any predator who targets children will have zero safe haven in this country or anywhere they try to hide,” Patel added. If convicted, Markle would face a statutory maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison. He is expected to appear in court in Tampa on Friday. "This case highlights the importance of the involvement of the public, even if it's a family member or close friend, to be vigilant and speak up if they have information on individuals they suspect may be preying on and exploiting our children," said Patrick Grandy, the assistant director in charge of the FBI's Los Angeles Field Office. In October, it was reported that Markle was under investigation in the Philippines over allegations that he possessed child sexual abuse material. He has not been charged by police in the Philippines. The Sun first reported that his son, Meghan's half-brother Thomas Markle Jr., told Philippine police that after his father left the country in May, he discovered images of child sexual abuse material among boxes at his father's former home in Cebu. Markle Sr. denied those allegations, telling the Daily Mail on Oct. 23: "It's just a bunch of lies. It's sick." Markle is believed to have returned to the U.S. in May, after his left leg was amputated in the Philippines in December 2025.  In October, The Sun reported Markle moved into Maravida Senior Living care home, a facility which specializes in "memory care." Meghan Markle released a statement following the claims, saying she was "deeply distressed." She also revealed that in 2019 she received a copy of a letter containing "troubling" allegations about him, which had been sent to London's Metropolitan Police. "It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated," she said. British police subsequently said it had not shared the letter with other law enforcement agencies. According to the Sun on Sunday , Meghan was advised that speaking publicly could jeopardize any potential legal case. Addressing her decision to keep Archie and Lilibet away from their grandfather over the past few years, Meghan said that "any distance from my father, and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them." She added: "My sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children." Meghan reportedly wrote to her estranged father in December 2025 to tell him she was aware of child abuse allegations against him and would not allow him to meet his grandchildren. Meghan reportedly told her father the letter would be the last time he heard from her. articles.title: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production after years of poor sales
articles.summary: So long, Tesla ( TSLA ) Cybertruck, we hardly knew ye. Yes, it is official. The Tesla Cybertruck will soon be no more, per a post from CEO Elon Musk on his X account. "Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk wrote early Friday morning. For many in the industry, this isn't a surprise even with Musk's grand pronouncements about the vehicle. Musk once boasted that Cybertruck demand was " so far off the hook, you can't even see the hook ," and the company said it had over 1 million preorders. Tesla CEO Elon Musk introduces the Cybertruck at Tesla's design studio in Hawthorne, Calif on Thursday, Nov. 21, 2019.  (AP Photo/Ringo H.W. Chiu, File) ASSOCIATED PRESS But conversion to sales never materialized. Cox Automotive's Kelley Blue Book estimated overall sales for the controversial pickup only hit around 71,000 since the vehicle went on sale in 2023. Tesla and Musk had built out capacity for Giga Austin to pump out 250K Cybertrucks per year; Tesla was selling about one-tenth that amount. When the truck was first revealed in late 2019 , Musk had promised a sub-$40,000 price tag for the cheapest version, and up to 500 miles of range for the top-end model. None of these things materialized. Tesla had wanted to get the first models out by late 2021, but delays in finalizing design, creating the large stainless steel body panels, and, of course, the pandemic delayed its release. Now, after a near four-year run (by mid 2027), the Cybertruck is no more. Musk and Tesla point to the need to boost production of the upcoming Cybercab, which has been testing in certain robotaxi markets. The Cybercab — which has no steering wheel or pedals — is a huge bet on autonomy and essentially ride-sharing as opposed to private ownership (though Tesla says the Cybercab will eventually go on sale to consumers). The Cybertruck's discontinuation comes after the cancellation of the Model S sedan and Model X SUV, two of Tesla's most significant — though pricey — models. At the time, Musk said the space at its Fremont factory where the S and X were made was needed for Optimus robot lines. Now the EV truck space has a bit more clarity. Rivian's R1T pickup and GM’s Chevrolet Silverado/GMC Sierra EV are now the only options; however, Ford will soon release the Fathom compact EV pickup . Then there's Slate , the startup with a no-frills, bare-bones $25K pickup. Musk's soaring vision of Tesla as a robotics, software, and autonomy company is becoming clear. But many Tesla fans who enjoy driving their own vehicles may be concerned about what happens to the company's remaining EVs for sale — if the bet for Tesla is on tech rather than cars. Pras Subramanian is the lead auto reporter for Yahoo Finance. You can follow him on X and on Instagram . articles.title: GOP's losses will raise pressure on conservative Supreme Court justices to retire
articles.summary: The GOP’s sweeping losses in the midterm elections Tuesday set up an unsettling possibility for the party: If it doesn’t act now to confirm a new Supreme Court justice, it may not have another chance for years to come. That prospect is likely to ramp up pressure on the court’s two oldest conservatives - Justices Samuel A. Alito Jr., 76, and Clarence Thomas, 78 - to retire during the lame-duck period, while Republicans still have the votes to get a nominee confirmed by the Senate. The new Senate, in which Democrats will hold a majority, is seated on Jan. 3. Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post. Alito, who joined the court in 2006, said last month he has no plans to retire during the lame-duck session. Thomas has said in the past he has no plans to step down from the court. He joined the court in 1991 and could become the longest-serving justice in its history in 2028. But given the magnitude of Democratic inroads in the Senate, legal and political experts said it could be 2033 before Republicans have a realistic shot at winning back enough seats in that chamber to approve a conservative justice. At that point, Alito and Thomas would be well into their 80s. Neither responded to a request for comment. “I think both have been making an implicit bet that they will live long enough … so that a Republican president can replace them with someone ideologically similar,” said Ed Whelan, a conservative attorney and senior fellow at the Ethics and Public Policy Center. This is likely to make many Republicans antsy, particularly those mindful of the lesson of Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, who died while still on the bench at 87, in September 2020. The liberal justice’s death allowed Republicans to move the court in a more conservative direction when they confirmed Justice Amy Coney Barrett to replace her weeks later. President Donald Trump nominated Barrett to replace Ginsburg, and over the vociferous objections of Democrats, Senate Republicans quickly muscled the nomination through just ahead of the 2020 presidential election. Trump remade the court with three picks in his first term - Barrett, Neil M. Gorsuch and Brett M. Kavanaugh - who pushed the court sharply to the right. The Supreme Court’s conservative 6-3 supermajority has delivered historic opinions on abortion, affirmative action, religious rights and much more that have thrilled Republicans. A younger replacement for Alito or Thomas could lock that advantage in for years to come. Liberals accused Republicans of hypocrisy for rapidly confirming Barrett after they blocked President Barack Obama’s nomination of Merrick Garland for 11 months in 2016, saying it was too close to the presidential election to confirm him. Trump won the White House, and Garland’s nomination was scuttled. Some observers think the window has already closed for Trump to nominate a fourth justice, which would allow him to leave a mark on the Supreme Court that few presidents have enjoyed. Republicans control 53 seats in the upper chamber, compared with 47 held by Democrats. But that split will shift to 52-48 as soon as Dec. 15, when Sen.-elect Sherrod Brown (D-Ohio) is seated as a result of a special election. A handful of moderate Senate Republicans like Maine’s Susan Collins and Alaska’s Lisa Murkowski might also have to be persuaded to back a Trump pick. The margin of error is thin enough that Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis (R) posted Tuesday night on X that Trump probably won’t be able to get a suitable nominee confirmed. “Chance of confirming a worthy successor to Justice Thomas and/or Alito during President Trump’s term: Zero,” DeSantis wrote. “Chance of confirming a worthy successor during a hypothetical GOP admin 2029-2033: probably zero (GOP won’t be able to recapture enough seats in 28).” Harry Litman, a law professor at UCLA and a former U.S. attorney, said the optics of a justice retiring during the lame-duck session would also tarnish his or her reputation. “It would be the most crass and nakedly political resignation in the court’s history,” Litman said. Emily Hampsten, a spokeswoman for Sen. Dick Durbin (Illinois), the Democratic whip and a member of the Judiciary Committee, said a lame-duck nominee would create a backlash among voters and Democrats. “The American people will hold them accountable in 2028, and Democrats could justifiably refuse to confirm any Trump nominees for the next two years,” Hampsten said. That would curtail one of Trump’s other biggest legacies - the nomination of hundreds of lower court federal judges. Steve Vladeck, a Georgetown law professor, wrote on his blog that a lame-duck confirmation fight might also backfire on the GOP by building support for court reforms that Democrats are already eyeing during the next Congress. “The question would no longer be whether the Court deserves to be restructured, but whether the other side has left Democrats any choice,” Vladeck wrote. Gabe Roth, executive director of the reform group Fix the Court, said he thinks only small reforms will be possible while Trump is still president over the next two years. “Democrats would do well to focus on areas within the realm of court reform where there’s already strong bipartisan support,” Roth said. “That includes banning stock trading in the federal courts, adding more lower court judgeships to relieve ballooning caseloads, improving workplace conduct protections for judiciary staff and making access to court records free.” Speculation over whether Alito would retire flared over the summer when NPR published an erroneous account saying he was planning on stepping down. The story was later retracted. Alito said during a round of interviews to promote his new book last month that he had no plans to retire during the current term, which will end in June or July. The justice said he has more to contribute to the court but did consider whether to continue each term. “I intend to stick around through this term,” Alito said in the interview before the Supreme Court’s new term began last month. “I made that decision many months ago.” Related Content This article originally appeared on Washington Post at https://washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/11/05/gops-losses-will-raise-pressure-conservative-supreme-court-justices-retire/

articles.title: Vance faces a 2028 dilemma as Republicans question his ties to Trump
articles.summary: The fight for the 2028 Republican primary is beginning to take shape on the heels of the GOP's devastating midterm losses, with Vice President Vance facing criticism for blaming the losses on the Iran war and other big-name Republicans appearing to stake out their own positions. The losses have created a huge opening for GOP White House hopefuls, including Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis and Sen. Ted Cruz (Texas), to go against Vance. It’s a fact seemingly recognized by Vance, who was quick to blame the Iran war for the historic drubbings, and Republicans at large. “The election results were bad news for every leader across the party, given the scale of the losses, but they were particularly tough for Vance’s 2028 prospects,” said Kevin Madden, the veteran Republican strategist who served as a senior adviser on Mitt Romney's 2012 presidential campaign. “Vance is now in the position of serving as a loyal vice president to a lame-duck president whose approval rating is in the 30’s and whose influence on the future of the party could be in question,” Madden added. Vance has long been seen as the front-runner to succeed President Trump as the GOP standard-bearer. A close second has been Secretary of State Marco Rubio. But questions are now being raised by Republicans over whether a candidate not directly tied to the administration would be stronger. “Tuesday made clear that the stink on Vice President Vance and Secretary [Marco] Rubio may be too much to overcome as the election was a referendum on the job they are doing,” said one top GOP operative who has spoken to DeSantis. “This certainly creates a lane for DeSantis, Cruz and others if they are willing to run in a potentially impossible year to win,” the operative added. In blaming the losses on Iran, Vance put some daylight between himself and his boss. Trump, for his part, has doubled down in insisting his administration made the right decision to start the war. “Vance’s profile as a candidate is directly tied to the Trump legacy. A candidate for 2028 without an ability to craft a more unique, independent profile of their own will face challenges in this next two-year cycle,” Madden predicted. The GOP operative who spoke to The Hill said 2028 “is going to be a difficult year for Republican presidential contenders if there aren’t substantial changes.” If there aren’t changes, the operative said DeSantis might wait until 2032 to run for president. DeSantis over the last 48 hours or so has certainly sounded like someone with the White House on his mind. The Florida governor, who unsuccessfully challenged Trump for the Republican nomination in 2024, was among the first this week to offer his own pointed view on what went wrong for GOP candidates, pointing to the war in Iran and high gas prices. In an interview with SiriusXM host Stephen A. Smith, he accused some in his party of “gaslighting” voters by not acknowledging their economic anxiety. DeSantis has also pointed out that the red wall in Florida, where the GOP won a Senate race and a gubernatorial contest, held. That’s an argument that would seem to point toward his leadership of the state. Republicans did lose three House races in districts that were redrawn to give GOP candidates an edge, and they are behind in a fourth. The gubernatorial and Senate races were also closer than expected. But DeSantis can certainly make an argument about his state being a GOP bastion. Cruz ahead of the elections had been more transparent about his ambition to run for president, saying he would entertain the idea of a 2028 run after the midterms. On his podcast, Cruz compared the losses to the drubbing Republicans took after Watergate, a comparison that would seem to at least raise the issue of corruption as being a factor in the GOP’s terrible night. He also criticized the Trump tariffs and the Iran war for raising costs. “Food is too high. Gas is too high. Diesel is too high. Insurance is too high. Life is too high,” he said. GOP strategists predict that after Tuesday’s results, their primary will be wide open. “Vance is completely unacceptable to any Republican who can accurately assess the reasons for the pasting we received on Tuesday,” one former Trump campaign aide said. “It not only opens the door for others, it should soundly shut the door for JD Vance.” Other Republicans say Tuesday’s results force Vance to stake his claim early or face the consequences of a more crowded field. “Vance needs to announce first with the president’s endorsement,” said Susan Del Percio, the veteran Republican strategist. “If he doesn’t do it in January, it’ll look like a sign of weakness and everyone will know the president isn’t on board. And that’s the million dollar question: Is he out of favor with the president?” One former Trump aide — who asked for anonymity to offer a candid assessment — said that right now, there’s “more space than less space” for other Republicans to enter the race. “Let’s face it, Cruz and DeSantis were the winners in our party the other night,” the former aide said. “This is absolutely the beginning of the end of the Trump era." The former aide added that Trump “is still going to be a potent force in the primary. If he endorses you, that’s 30 percent right off the bat." But the former aide predicted it would be difficult for Vance to keep his distance from Trump and that he would be pigeonholed to his stances. “Imagine, he’s going to have to answer to Trump’s whim or rant of the day every day,” the former aide said. “And he’s not going to stand in stark contrast to the president because Trump will shred him. “That’s just not an enviable place,” the former aide added. Since the elections, Vance has been under scrutiny from both Republicans and Democrats. Former White House press secretary Ari Fleischer, who served under former President George W. Bush, took to social platform X to counter Vance’s evaluation of the sweeping GOP losses. “Please allow me to present a different perspective,” Fleischer said. “The problem was not the Iran War. It was the cease fire. If you start a war, you need to win it and finish it - otherwise don’t start it.” Democrats also pounced on Vance’s remarks. “For you to reduce it to a simple political calculation while we still have 50,000 troops in the Middle East, is one of the most crass, cynical things I’ve seen,” Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.), wrote Wednesday on X. “You and President Trump got us into this war without a clear objective and without regard for the will of the American people. It’s cost us American lives and billions of dollars of American treasure with no end in sight.” On Thursday, as political pundits were saying it was the end of the Trump era, Republicans said Vance’s political future remained murky at best. “I think if you’re Vance you gotta take the nomination and pray you get someone on the other side like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez,” the first former Trump aide said, referring to the progressive representative from New York. For now, Del Percio said, results aside, Vance “ultimately stands in the same place he did three weeks ago.” “He only exists at the whim of the president,” she said. “And if Trump doesn’t endorse, will Vance go without the president’s endorsement? If he’s forced to do that, he will break with Trump and it will get ugly.” Copyright 2026 Nexstar Media, Inc. All rights reserved. articles.title: Data centers get blamed for soaring electric bills. A new study points elsewhere.
articles.summary: On Tuesday, Americans voted overwhelmingly against data centers and artificial intelligence growth. In 40 of 41 local ballot races around the country, many in the state of Ohio, voters opted to restrict or prohibit new data center constructions in their areas. Much of the growing opposition to data centers has come from rising electricity prices , which are squeezing Americans in a time of already high prices and cost of living. But, according to a new study by researchers at Harvard University and the University of Pennsylvania, data centers are probably having only a small effect on residential electricity prices. The researchers calculated that these operations were responsible for just 4 percent of the utility rate increases over the last five years. Get Climate Coach newsletter News and guidance on climate, science and technology. Sign up for free “Even to me it was somewhat surprising,” said Serguei Netessine, professor at the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania and one of the study’s authors. In the run-up to the elections, Democrats pointed to data centers — and Republican support for their development — as key drivers of electricity price increases. In one campaign ad , Democrat James Talarico, now senator-elect of Texas, said that Texans were “paying the price with skyrocketing utility bills.” Sherrod Brown, Democratic senator-elect of Ohio, similarly argued that state residents were facing higher electricity bills due to the build-out of energy-hogging data centers. There are certainly some areas — like in Pennsylvania, Virginia, Ohio and other states covered by grid operator PJM — where data centers have skyrocketed demand, pushing some costs onto residential customers. But multiple studies by different researchers and organizations have failed to find a strong connection between data centers and the overall trajectory of U.S. electricity prices in recent years. Another analysis earlier this year by researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology found that, between 2010 and 2024, data centers increased average electricity prices for residential customers by just 2.1 percent. Last year, research from the Brattle Group and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory found that data centers were actually decreasing costs in certain regions. And another study by the Electric Power Research Institute found that a doubling of data center capacity between 2019 and 2024 resulted in a 4 percent drop in home electricity prices. Most Read From The Washington Post Sullivan and Peltola remain neck-and-neck in Alaska Senate race Colom’s lead grows over Hyde-Smith in Mississippi race amid legal saber-rattling Hegseth not under consideration to be appointed to Senate Judge halts Trump’s arch after federal panel approves it Republicans in North Carolina lose 4 more House seats as GOP wipeout spreads “Depending on which techniques you use, you can identify a slight increase or decrease in prices historically” due to data centers, said Ryan Hledik, principal at the Brattle Group. “None of these are the kind of earth-shattering rate impacts you hear about.” The new Harvard and Penn study found a slightly higher impact on industrial electricity prices — the price paid by manufacturers and large facilities. For those customers, data centers were responsible for 15 percent of the price increase between 2020 and 2025. But for ordinary Americans, Netessine said, the changes simply were not substantial. “So far we have no evidence that data centers increase prices all that much,” Netessine said. Instead, he said, prices are rising due to more quotidian factors: rising gas prices, an aging electricity grid, and wildfires and hurricanes requiring improvements to the grid and recovery after disaster. Most of the cost of generating and delivering electricity is based on large, up-front capital costs, such as the costs to build power plants, wires and transmission lines to carry that power into homes. Some areas of the United States also have excess “capacity” in the grid — meaning that the grid is overbuilt for the actual demand. In those areas, adding a data center means that large fixed grid costs are spread over more consumers. That could lower prices. Of course, that’s not the case everywhere. PJM has had booming data center growth that has also required additional build-out of the power grid. This has raised prices at power capacity auctions, and states like Maryland have seen increasing residential prices that are at least in part from this boom. If the number of data centers continue to boom, experts say, residential prices could be affected more down the line. Data center electricity demand is expected to increase steeply over the next few years, requiring new power generation — wind, solar or natural gas — to be put onto the grid. And residents have issues with data centers that go beyond the price of electricity. The new developments have been singled out for loud noise , polluting power generation , and for disturbing residential neighborhoods and natural landscapes. According to the Pew Research Center, more than half of Americans say that data centers are mostly bad for the environment. Others feel that the AI race — which could ultimately leave many Americans out of work — is being forced upon them. “I think generally what we’re seeing is a broader range of reasons the public has opposed data centers,” Hledik said. “Concern about AI leading to loss of jobs — all of that is getting packaged together.” This article originally appeared on Washington Post at https://www.washingtonpost.com/climate-environment/2026/11/06/data-centers-may-not-be-raising-americans-electricity-bills-that-much/

articles.title: SpaceX大反弹逾9%，马斯克放话：Q4营收料将增长70%，明年剑指5000亿
articles.summary: SpaceX股价周五大幅反弹，马斯克在巴伦投资大会上发出一系列乐观信号，提振市场情绪。 周五美股尾盘，SpaceX股价上涨9.1%，报134.91美元，创下自8月12日以来的最大单日涨幅。这一反弹发生在此前两个交易日大跌9%之后。 据彭博社报道，马斯克在巴伦年度投资大会上表示， SpaceX第四季度营收将较第三季度增长约70%，并重申公司有望在12月实现1000亿美元的年化营收规模，到2027年底该数字将突破5000亿美元。 与此同时，马斯克披露，SpaceX来自美国政府机构的收入本季度将降至不足总营收的10%，低于上一季度的16.6%。 分析认为，这一表态标志着SpaceX正加速摆脱对政府合同的依赖，转型为一家以人工智能和卫星业务为核心驱动力的商业科技公司，对投资者评估其未来收入结构具有重要参考意义。 政府合同占比持续下滑，AI业务跃升为第一大收入来源 SpaceX与美国政府机构的合作曾是其最重要的收入来源，但这一格局正在迅速改变。 据彭博报道，2025年全年，来自政府机构的合同约占SpaceX总营收的五分之一。而在 最近一个季度，该比例已降至16.6% ， 马斯克预计本季度将进一步降至10%以下。 马斯克在X平台回应用户时表示，SpaceX获得的政府合同"产品最好、价格最低"，并暗示即便民主党议员有异议，公司也无惧取消合同。 尽管如此，SpaceX与政府的合作仍具战略重要性。公司目前持有NASA将人类送上月球的关键合同，计划使用Starship火箭最早于2028年执行载人登月任务。 同时，五角大楼也依赖SpaceX发射重要的国家安全卫星。竞争对手此前曾抱怨，国防部的合同设计过于针对性，实际上只有SpaceX能够赢得。 此外，马斯克还表示，若有机会收购一家大型无线运营商，主要目的将是获取其宝贵的频谱资源 。SpaceX过去一年已购入两批无线频段，用于推进其星地混合无线网络建设。 相比之下，AI客户正迅速主导SpaceX的收入结构。据彭博报道，AI公司Anthropic目前已是SpaceX的单一最大客户，贡献了超过三分之一的季度营收。SpaceX还与Alphabet旗下谷歌等科技企业签有算力租赁合同。 马斯克在上一季度财报电话会议上表示，位于田纳西州孟菲斯的数据中心算力需求持续攀升，AI业务本季度首次实现盈利。 股价承压背景复杂，AI算力合同稳定性受质疑 尽管周五反弹强劲，SpaceX股价在更长周期内仍面临压力。 数据显示，该股过去五个交易日累计下跌10.32%，过去一个月跌幅达28.13%，距去年约226美元的历史高点已大幅回落。 交易员Ali Martinez指出，SPCX已跌破其平行交易通道的中轨，若进一步下行，可能面临再跌12%至108美元区域的风险，逼近历史低点104.83美元。 Martinez还将近期抛压部分归因于10月一批约20亿股的股票解禁，额外供给压力对股价形成拖累。 SpaceX正大力押注的AI算力租赁业务也并非没有风险 。据彭博报道，微软正逐步终止与甲骨文之间的数据中心使用协议，凸显出算力合同的脆弱性。此外，SpaceX最大客户Anthropic最快可能于明年通过通知期后退出合作协议。 值得注意的是，马斯克本次发布预测，距民主党重新掌控参众两院仅数日。这位亿万富翁在选举周期内为共和党斥资逾4.45亿美元，外界关注此举是否会对SpaceX与新一届国会的政府合同关系造成潜在影响。 马斯克称Model Y已成全球最畅销车型 在同一场巴伦大会上，马斯克还就旗下另一家公司特斯拉发表了重要表态。 马斯克宣布，特斯拉Model Y已成为全球销量最高的车型，覆盖燃油车和电动车所有类别。他特别点出中国市场，称Model Y是中国最畅销的电动车，并直言"中国车企非常厉害"，对本土竞争对手的技术实力给予罕见的公开认可。 马斯克表示，在全球最大汽车市场与国内品牌的激烈竞争中守住领先位置，本身就说明了Model Y的产品竞争力。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: AI“新云”超跌反弹迅速降温！CoreWeave一度由涨转跌，IREN涨幅腰斩
articles.summary: 经历前一交易日的猛烈抛售后，AI算力基础设施股票周五一度迎来强劲反弹，但盘中涨势明显降温。 CoreWeave由早盘一度上涨9.3%转为下跌，IREN涨幅从盘初的24.6%收窄至约12%，Nebius Group也从一度上涨13.7%回落至约2.4%。截至发稿，CoreWeave周五上涨4.4%。 这轮反弹最初受到IREN最新财报提振。该公司AI Cloud业务收入大幅增长，季度营收超过市场预期，为近期遭到重挫的Neocloud板块提供了积极信号。 不过，财报同时暴露出数据中心项目交付延期、资本开支高企等问题，市场对行业扩张成本和盈利兑现能力的担忧并未消退。 周四，AI基础设施股票遭遇大幅抛售。美国中期选举结果引发市场对数据中心建设监管趋严的担忧，叠加 微软收紧对部分Neocloud供应商项目的审查 ，CoreWeave、Nebius和IREN分别下跌约10%、15%和17%。 周五的反弹虽然显示部分资金开始回补仓位， 美股午盘微软继续被曝 逐步关闭此前从甲骨文租用的部分计算资源 ，并决定不再续签相关合同。 消息传出后，甲骨文股价迅速跳水，此前大幅反弹的Neocloud概念股也纷纷回吐涨幅。 IREN财报超预期，成为板块反弹催化剂 IREN周四盘后公布的2027财年第一季度业绩为板块带来一定提振。 截至9月30日的季度， IREN实现营收2.28亿美元，高于分析师预期的2.21亿美元。其中，AI Cloud业务营收达到2亿美元，较上一季度的7100万美元大幅增长。 公司调整后EBITDA为6600万美元。 IREN还披露，其收入积压订单达到203亿美元，反映出AI算力需求仍为业务扩张提供支撑。 业绩公布后，投资者重新评估Neocloud企业的增长前景。IREN股价盘初一度上涨约24.6%，CoreWeave和Nebius也跟随反弹。 不过，强劲的收入增长并未完全消除市场对IREN执行能力的疑虑。 公司表示，由于微软要求调整网络设计，以及供应商交付时间安排发生变化，部分数据中心基础设施交付出现延期。IREN原计划在年底实现超过40亿美元的年化收入运行率目标，现在将时间推迟至2027年1月，甚至可能延后至2月底。 与此同时，IREN预计本财年剩余时间资本开支约150亿美元。截至9月底，公司资本承诺已达到189.5亿美元，较三个月前的138.1亿美元明显增加。 这意味着，AI Cloud业务的高速增长仍需要持续投入大量资金，而项目延期也可能推迟相关收入的兑现时间。 微软连续两天释放收缩信号，不再续租甲骨文部分算力 周四，彭博报道称，微软正在加强对Nebius、IREN和Nscale部分数据中心项目的监督，并退出其认为风险较高的项目，同时在内部讨论是否继续签署新的Neocloud合作协议。 周五美股午盘，彭博援引知情人士再次报道称，微软近几个月已开始逐步关闭此前从甲骨文租用的部分计算资源，并决定不再续签相关合同。 报道指出， 随着时间推移，微软租用的计算资源逐渐无法满足其不断变化的技术需求。甲骨文相关服务器搭载的是较早一代英伟达芯片，其对微软的使用价值因此下降。 消息公布后，甲骨文股价迅速由涨转跌，早盘一度上涨3.8%，随后抹平涨幅并刷新日内低点至109.21美元，盘中跌幅一度接近5.2%。 甲骨文方面则强调，公司仍然看到市场对AI基础设施的旺盛需求，包括对较早一代GPU的需求。 这一消息也迅速传导至AI算力租赁概念股。CoreWeave、IREN和Nebius均在早盘大幅反弹后出现明显回落。 相关报道进一步加剧了市场对第三方算力供应商商业模式的担忧。 对于CoreWeave、Nebius和IREN等企业而言，业务扩张高度依赖数据中心建设、GPU采购以及外部融资。它们需要在项目产生收入之前投入大量资金，因此，电力接入延误、设备交付推迟或客户调整需求，都可能影响收入确认和资金回收周期。 融资环境同样构成压力。尤其是CoreWeave，其高杠杆扩张模式已经受到信用市场关注。在AI基础设施投资回报周期仍存在不确定性的背景下，投资者对资本密集型企业的估值容忍度正在下降。 民主党胜选引发政策担忧，市场重新审视AI基建投资回报 除了企业自身的经营问题，政策环境变化也是近期板块剧烈波动的重要背景。 美国民主党在中期选举中取得重大胜利后，市场开始担心数据中心建设可能面临更严格的监管审查。得克萨斯州等重要数据中心市场的政策走向尤其受到关注。 据路透援引UBS分析师估计，美国2028年预期新增数据中心容量中，约30%可能面临建设暂停风险。 在此背景下， 周五早盘的反弹更多受到业绩超预期、科技股整体回升以及前一日大幅下跌后的仓位修复推动。而微软最新披露的算力租赁调整，再度将市场注意力拉回第三方算力供应商的客户需求、技术迭代和资本回报问题。 对于CoreWeave、IREN和Nebius而言，AI算力需求增长仍然提供长期业务机会，但大型云服务商能否持续扩大外部采购，以及供应商能否按期交付符合技术要求的算力，正在成为影响行业估值的重要变量。 articles.title: 大金主踩刹车？OpenAI新融资被曝遇冷、软银大幅缩减投入，CFO称中选后数据中心投资不变
articles.summary: OpenAI正面临新一轮融资的重大挑战。在10月末传出OpenAI将 融资目标调低100亿美元 的消息后，本周五又有《纽约时报》的报道称，多位主要投资方在本轮融资中大幅削减出资规模，软银等此前最积极的支持者此次仅计划投入数亿美元，与过往数百亿美元的投入相比不可同日而语。 据今年10月末的《金融时报》报道，OpenAI将本轮融资目标从最初的300亿美元削减至少三分之一，目前寻求融资规模约为200亿美元，估值也从最高1.5万亿美元下调至1.25万亿美元。据《纽约时报》DealBook本周五的报道，本轮OpenAI融资分两部分进行，第一部分截止日期为11月6日周五当天，预计实际募集金额将低于200亿美元。 同在周五，OpenAI首席财务官Sarah Friar在花旗TMT领导力峰会上接受CNBC采访时表示，尽管本周结束的中期选举中许多选民投票反对数据中心建设，OpenAI仍将继续推进数据中心基础设施投资，并确认融资进程仍在进行中。她表示，"一位优秀的CFO总是在能融资的时候融资"，并重申公司仍在考虑2027年上市。 Friar讲话前一天，OpenAI已作出改变数据中心项目推进方式的姿态，当天发布“全国社区契约”框架，承诺数据中心项目不签保密协议、不将电力成本转嫁给居民。OpenAI首席全球事务官Chris Lehane表示，部分项目存在推迟的可能，并坦承选民的投票表达是企业必须倾听和回应的重要信号。 主要投资方出资意愿明显降温 据DealBook本周五援引知情人士消息，本轮融资中，阿联酋投资者联合体（包括国有科技基金MGX）预计将成为最大出资方，承诺出资金额为单位数的十亿美元级别。 软银的态度转变尤为引人关注。这家日本企业集团此前是OpenAI最积极的支持者之一，迄今已累计向OpenAI投入约650亿美元，其中包括今年3月参与的1220亿美元融资轮中的300亿美元，以及2025年3月400亿美元融资轮中的300亿美元。然而据知情人士透露，软银此次仅在商讨投入数亿美元。 现有投资方Coatue同样计划缩减出资规模。据两位知情人士告知DealBook，Coatue此次讨论的投资金额也在数亿美元级别。值得注意的是，Coatue同时也是OpenAI竞争对手Anthropic的投资方。 市场动荡与竞争压力构成双重逆风 本轮融资遭遇的阻力，与近期科技股的大幅回调密切相关。据CNBC报道，纳斯达克指数周四录得19个月来最大单日跌幅，芯片制造商及与AI基础设施建设关联最紧密的新兴云计算公司股价领跌，周五有所反弹。 投资者对AI交易的态度趋于谨慎，背后是借贷成本上升、债务规模持续攀升以及公众对AI行业的反弹情绪等多重因素叠加。据金融时报10月底报道，一位OpenAI支持者表示，融资启动之初市场对AI交易热情高涨，但随后遭遇市场急剧逆转。 与此同时，竞争对手Anthropic的上市计划也在分流投资者的注意力与资金。Anthropic计划于11月中旬登陆纳斯达克，目标估值达1.5万亿美元或更高。由于两家公司面向相似的投资者群体，OpenAI此前急于在Anthropic上市前完成本轮融资。据Anthropic招股书显示，该公司今年前九个月营收同比增长约1200%，达332亿美元。 CFO：数据中心投资不会停步，IPO目标不变 尽管融资环境趋紧，Sarah Friar在CNBC采访中仍对公司前景表达了明确立场。 她表示，中期选举结果不会从根本上改变公司的战略方向——在41项涉及数据中心的地方选票中，选民对绝大多数支持数据中心建设的议案投了反对票，但Friar表示，"如果中期选举意味着更多关注数据中心与社区关系，我们将继续深入这些社区、建立信任。" 在IPO进程方面，Friar确认OpenAI已于今年6月向美国证券交易委员会秘密提交招股说明书，并表示公司将继续推进2027年上市计划。她同时强调，"对AI的需求是真实存在的"，并将本轮持续融资定性为满足客户需求、维持基础设施投入的必要举措。 OpenAI表示，预计本轮融资将在未来数周内完成。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 1998 VS 2000，高盛主管：AI抛售更像LTCM危机而非互联网泡沫，但关键问题尚未解答
articles.summary: 市场正在经历一场关于历史先例的激烈辩论：这究竟是1998年长期资本管理公司（LTCM）危机式的流动性冲击，还是2000年互联网泡沫破裂的序幕？高盛Delta One交易主管Rich Privorotsky倾向于前者，但他自己也承认，决定性答案尚未到来。 周四，纳斯达克单日暴跌5.5%，费城半导体指数重挫12%，标普500下跌4.4%，创下2025年4月以来最大单日跌幅。高盛波动性恐慌指数当日触及10分满分中的9.3分，VVIX单日飙升近45点，创有史以来第二大单日涨幅，仅次于2018年的"波动末日"事件。 触发因素是民主党横扫选举后市场对数据中心建设前景的重新定价，导火索是德克萨斯州等多个州对数据中心建设的潜在监管限制。 这场抛售引发的核心问题，正在成为每一位基金经理的灵魂之问：AI投资热潮的基本逻辑是否依然完好，还是市场正在揭示一个在经济上根本站不住脚的叙事？ 程序主导的机械性抛售 周四的暴跌，从市场结构层面看，是一次机械性事件与基本面冲击的叠加。 Privorotsky指出，杠杆ETF在半导体板块和纳斯达克100指数收盘前触发了机械性卖盘，叠加负向做市商Gamma头寸，共同形成"自我强化的清仓效应"。 野村证券的Charlie McElligott估算， 当日杠杆ETF卖出规模达470亿美元，波动率控制基金供应量达610亿美元，做市商对于标普每下跌1%持有约70亿美元的负Gamma敞口。 高盛美国销售交易员Ariana Contessa在当日流动与持仓报告中补充道，VIX单日跳升67%至27.77，高盛多个AI相关篮子当天创下ChatGPT推出以来最大单日跌幅。 而程序的抛售尚未结束——期货收盘跌破CTA中期阈值7549点， 据高盛下行2.5个标准差情景测算，未来一周标普500面临逾74.8亿美元的程序性卖盘压力 ；瑞银则警告，风险控制基金仅当日卖盘或超过1000亿美元。 真正的问题：买盘缺席 程序卖盘制造了价格压力，但Privorotsky认为，真正令人担忧的是另一面——买盘的消失。 高盛现金股票部门当日净卖出30亿美元，其中科技股占22亿美元，将科技板块净卖出规模累计推至270亿美元，已超过2025年7月那轮技术性调整的210亿美元。 Contessa描述，来自客户的问询强度"满分10分"，但实际成交活跃度"仅5分"，ETF占全天交易量的32%。 尤其值得注意的是，周三曾为指数托底的超大型科技股（Hyperscalers）"完全没有看到对应的买盘出现"。 Privorotsky的诊断直白而犀利： "真正的问题是底层需求的缺席，尤其是来自长线基金的需求……感觉多策略、量化、长线基金和散户都在同一方向，这正是问题所在。" 1998还是2000：Privorotsky的倾向与保留 面对市场最关键的定性之争，Privorotsky明确表达了立场，但并未回避内心的不安。 他倾向1998年的LTCM危机类比： 俄罗斯违约和LTCM崩盘是当年的外部冲击，但美国经济增长基本面保持完好，一旦流动性恢复、美联储降息，市场迅速收复失地。 他认为，今日的AI增长引擎或许同样完好，市场只是在激烈地重新定价建设融资节奏与时间表。 支撑这一判断的核心论据是估值与资产负债表。Privorotsky指出，与2000年不同，当前科技巨头拥有真实的营收、现金流和强健的资产负债表。 高盛TMT交易员Peter Callahan指出，半导体指数的估值倍数相比6月至7月高点已压缩约50%， 英伟达的未来24个月滚动市盈率约为10倍，为2013年以来最低。相比之下，2000年思科的市盈率超过100倍——这是支持1998年类比最有力的论据。 然而，Privorotsky也坦诚地列出了令他夜不能寐的另一面： "与2000年令人不安的相似之处在于 资本支出规模之庞大，以及回报的高度不确定性。 我们究竟是在清仓一个健康的增长故事，还是在发现这个故事的经济逻辑本身就是错的？我倾向于前者，但需求、利用率和回报必须经受住考验。" 四大隐忧，市场盯错了方向 Privorotsky将此次AI抛售背后的担忧分解为四个层次：一是融资能力不足以支撑建设规模；二是营收不足以证明资本投入的合理性；三是电力与许可产能不足以支撑算力扩张；四是整体资本开支轨迹不可持续。 他的判断是，市场此刻执着于第三点——电力与许可，"可以说是这四者中最不重要的"。 受限的供给并不等于需求消失，真正的问题是营收能否最终匹配所投入的资本。 然而，第一点"融资"正在闪烁红色警报。据高盛IR团队统计，超大型科技公司今年已发行2960亿美元债券，高于高盛此前全年2500亿美元的预测，占全球所有货币投资级债券供应总量的约9%。 与此同时，数据中心信用违约掉期（CDS）周四突破500个基点，创历史新高；CoreWeave债券利差则超过1200个基点。 Privorotsky所指出的，恰恰是一个结构性的恶性循环：电力许可的延误（第三点）正在直接推高融资成本（第一点）。每一个季度的许可延迟，都意味着一座半建好的数据中心要多付一个季度的利息。 政治催化剂：德克萨斯州的监管信号 此次市场抛售的直接导火索，是选举结果引发的监管预期转变。高盛估算，各州层面的暂停令可能冻结约45%的美国计划数据中心产能，仅德克萨斯州便占其中约四分之一。 Privorotsky认为市场对德克萨斯州候任州长Gina Hinojosa的解读过于字面化。他援引她的表态——"我们既可以推动经济发展，也可以保护德克萨斯人的利益，二者并不互相排斥"，以及"我并不是痛恨数据中心"——得出判断： "这听起来更像是监管层面的重置，而非意识形态上的排斥。实际支出或许会超出目前市场折价所反映的预期。" 高盛IR团队补充称，据CNBC报道，Hinojosa已表示已取得许可的数据中心将被允许完工，这"可能保护了2027年乃至2028年的大部分建设进程"，高盛经济学家也预计相关暂停令将较为短暂，因为数据中心在选民优先级列表中排名靠后。 但不满情绪不容忽视。据Jefferies援引Heatmap调查数据，强烈反对在居所附近建设数据中心的美国民众比例，从2025年9月的24%飙升至2026年8月的61%。 乔治亚州、俄亥俄州和密歇根州正在跟进德克萨斯州的立法动向。德克萨斯州的立法会期截至5月31日，所谓"监管重置"，依然是一次真实的重置。 1998年剧本的缺陷：当下没有美联储的降息护航 Privorotsky以历史数据为底气收尾：自1950年以来19次中期选举后，标普500在未来12个月内均录得上涨，"这是12个月维度的观察，不是一个月的预测"。他认为此类事件历史上均构成买入机会，但短期内难以把握时机。 然而，1998年类比存在一个致命的内在矛盾，而这个矛盾就隐藏在Privorotsky自己对1998年的描述之中："一旦流动性恢复、美联储降息。" 1998年，时任美联储主席Greenspan在七周内三度降息。而在2026年，市场仍在定价约65%的概率押注美联储12月加息，克利夫兰联储的Hammack周四上午还在公开表达维持限制性立场的倾向。 这一次，不会有美联储召集的LTCM救援会议，而超大型科技公司今年已发行的2960亿美元债券，意味着这轮建设潮对债券市场的依赖程度前所未有。 流动性面也并不乐观。科技股多空基金今年以来收益基本持平，年末有强烈动机锁定现有成果；程序化卖盘仍在继续；Privorotsky本人也坦言，"真正的问题"在于长线基金买盘的缺失。 综合来看，1998年或许是正确的终点，但2000年可能是中途必经的路径——至少在有实质性买盘力量真正出场之前如此。唯一值得宽慰的，或许是这样一个对比：英伟达10倍远期市盈率，终究不是思科的100倍以上。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 首席风险官再离职！实力券商合并后的"人才洗牌"
articles.summary: 同一天，两份公告。 11月4日晚，国联民生同时披露两则消息：全资子公司民生证券参与国联期货换股吸收合并民生期货，民生期货解散注销，"一总部+八家专业子公司"架构就此收官； 同日，公司首席风险官江志强因工作调整辞职，辞职后不再在公司及控股子公司担任任何职务。由此带来了又一轮高管变动的契机。 谁是 江志强 ？ 江志强生于 1970年，是原国联证券体系成长起来的高管，他历任证券投资部经理、营业部总经理、财富管理中心总经理、资产管理部总经理、公司总裁助理、公司副总裁、监事会主席等。自2021年5月起担任公司首席风险官。 简历可以看出，江志强长期的深耕领域就是投资线和经纪业务线。这体现出他相对专业和市场化的两面。 值得提及的是，江志强在国联证券体系中又属于 “老国联”，即不属于2015年后加入的有中信证券工作背景的“新国联人”，这为他的简历打下稳定、长期的标签。 从身兼数职到彻底离开 江志强曾 长期连续担任母公司 国联民生证券 首席风险官，并同时兼任资管子公司 国联证券资产管理有限公司 首席风险官。 2025年10月，他曾因职务调整离任国联证券资管首席风险官； 同时，他也是国联民生证券的前身国联证券的首席风险官， 2021年上任，2025年12月，他因公司合并而被第六届国联民生证券董事会第一次会议聘为国联民生证券的首席风险官。 结果， 仅仅一年时间 ，他 彻底离开了效力多年的老东家 ，且此次公告明确写明辞职后不再在公司及控股子公司担任任何职务。公告给出的原因是 "工作调整"。 国联民生的 高管变动 小高潮 江志强的离任并非 个例 事件。梳理公告可以发现，过去三个多月里，公司高管层经历了密集变动， 这背后即有公司合并因素导致的变动，又有高管和公司双向主动调整的结果。 其中以公司总裁葛小波的离任，最为引人关注。因为后者几乎是 “中信系”人才团队的领头人，却在远未到退休年龄时离开，令人扼腕。 时间 变动 去向 2026.8.8 非执行董事杨振兴辞职 不在公司及控股子公司任职 2026.8.21 总裁葛小波辞去执行董事、总裁等全部职务 彻底退出管理层，媒体称下一站或为华兴资本 2026.8.21 汪锦岭代行总裁职责 10月29日新任执行董事 2026.9.18 副总裁胡又文辞职 继续以高管身份在研究所任职，研究所划入民生证券 2026.11.4 首席风险官江志强辞职 不再担任任何职务 值得关注的是， 2025年8月公司刚完成一轮高管聘任——熊雷鸣任执行副总裁、郑亮与胡又文任副总裁，马群星同期不再担任副总裁。也就是说，不到一年时间，这一批"刚上任"的人中已有部分离开或平移，"进"与"出"在同一批人身上交替出现。 人才 "洗牌" 效果值得观察 高管接连变动、骨干流失，这些人才 "洗牌"带来的影响，目前在国联民生证券的报表上还看不出来。 最新三季报显示，公司前三季度营收与净利润实现双增，回购计划与控股股东增持方案相继推出，说明架构整合目前在报表上更多的体现为正效应。 当然，这也是一家国联民生这样实力和梯队齐整的券商必然会表现的一面。长期来说，结果怎样，还需要时间的答案。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 10月非农重燃12月加息预期！华尔街押注概率超八成，“新美联储通讯社”：AI抛售或成政策变量
articles.summary: 美国10月非农就业数据强于预期，重新点燃华尔街押注美联储12月加息的热情。交易员在报告公布后预计，美联储12月加息25个基点的概率已升至八成以上。 美国劳工统计局（BLS）11月6日周五公布的数据显示，10月非农就业人数增加16.5万人，远超华尔街预期的增幅7万；失业率降至4.1%，劳动力参与率则升至61.9%，均未如市场所料持平9月；平均时薪环比上涨0.4%，较9月加快程度超出市场预期。就业、失业和薪资指标整体偏强。 多家华尔街机构人士认为，这份报告为美联储12月进一步加息提供了更充分的依据。不过，能源价格和后续通胀走势，以及近期AI相关资产抛售对金融条件的影响，仍可能左右美联储下一步行动。 有“新美联储通讯社”之称的记者Nick Timiraos认为，这份就业报告并未动摇美联储对经济增长和通胀的判断，但近期AI相关资产抛售是否会改变金融条件，可能成为12月政策决策中的另一重变量。美联储主席沃什究竟更看重滞后的就业数据，还是前瞻性的市场信号，成为接下来值得关注的焦点。 12月加息概率一度升至85% 华尔街认为强劲就业为美联储提供行动空间 就业报告公布后，利率市场迅速调整政策预期。报道显示，交易员对美联储12月会议加息25个基点的押注升至约85%，高于报告公布前的约75%；市场对下一次加息的预期时间也有所提前。 高盛资产管理多部门固定收益投资主管Lindsay Rosner认为，这份非农报告为美联储12月加息扫清了障碍。她表示：“这份非农数据移除了美联储在12月政策十字路口前的红绿灯。”就业市场持续收紧，为美联储进一步加息提供了空间，而且不必然损害其就业目标。 Franklin Templeton Institute首席投资策略师Jeff Schulze称，10月就业报告表现强劲，在中期选举后市场担忧AI建设放缓可能削弱加息预期的背景下，重新给美联储带来了加息压力。 IFM Investors的Ryan Weldon也认为，虽然在美联储12月会议前还将公布一份通胀报告，但经济表现强劲、通胀具有黏性，令美联储很难回避加息选项。 Fitch Ratings分析师Olu Sonola指出，这是一份非常强劲的劳动力市场报告。结合稳健的GDP和消费数据，美国经济目前仍具韧性，AI相关担忧尚未明显改变这一判断；随着就业市场表现坚挺，美联储的政策讨论可能进一步转向通胀和12月加息。 就业与薪资同步走强，但劳动力市场仍有结构性隐忧 10月非农新增就业16.5万人，不仅大幅超过市场预期，也是2026年以来仅次于3月和8月的第三高月度增幅。此前两个月的就业数据也获得上修：8月新增就业人数从13.3万人上修至18.6万人，9月从2.9万人上修至6万人，合计上修8.4万人。 从行业看，专业和商业服务业新增7万人，医疗保健业新增4.2万人，运输和仓储业新增2.5万人，制造业新增1.9万人；休闲和酒店业则减少1.3万人。专业和商业服务业就业增长明显加快，也为有关AI正在迅速侵蚀白领岗位的担忧提供了一个值得关注的反向信号。 High Frequency Economics首席经济学家Carl Weinberg认为，美国经济已经处于或非常接近充分就业状态。强劲的就业需求意味着，美联储需要关注劳动力需求是否正在超过供给。 薪资数据也强化了就业市场偏热的信号。10月平均时薪环比上涨0.4%，高于市场预期的0.3%，较9月0.1%的涨幅明显加快；同比增幅为3.1%。劳动力参与率也从9月的61.8%升至61.9%，并未出现就业增长完全由劳动力退出市场推动的情况。 不过，报告并非没有隐忧。因经济原因而被迫从事兼职工作的人数增加33.9万人，达到约484万人，显示部分劳动者仍无法获得理想的全职工作。 Annex Wealth Management首席经济策略师BRIAN JACOBSEN指出，尽管薪资同比增长3.1%，但如果通胀高于这一水平，劳动者的实际平均时薪仍会下降。他将这一现象称为“一个数字就呈现了可负担性危机”。在他看来，能源价格上涨推高生活成本，也可能进一步加大美联储的政策压力。 通胀和能源价格仍是加息路径的关键变量 尽管就业报告强化了12月加息预期，但华尔街人士并不认为单份就业数据就能决定美联储的政策路径。下一轮通胀数据、能源价格走势，以及高利率对金融市场和经济活动的影响，仍是关键变量。 High Frequency Economics首席经济学家Carl Weinberg认为，经济已处于或接近充分就业，美联储需要防范劳动力需求超过供给所带来的通胀风险。 Spartan Capital Securities首席市场经济学家PETER CARDILLO则认为，失业率降至4.1%、薪资涨幅高于预期，说明就业市场仍然强劲。他判断，美联储12月加息已很难回避，剩下的问题在于加息25个还是50个基点。 但ANSHUL SHARMA提醒，后续仍需关注通胀，尤其是能源价格。即使就业和薪资数据支持加息，如果能源价格回落、通胀压力减轻，美联储仍可能重新评估政策选择。 华尔街分歧：股市波动和AI投资前景可能牵制美联储 强劲就业数据推高了加息预期，但近期金融市场的波动也让部分市场人士对美联储是否会在12月采取行动保持谨慎。 Themis Trading联席主管JOE SALUZZI认为，新增就业、工资增速和此前数据修订均表现强劲，确实提高了美联储下一次加息的可能性。不过，前一日股市波动率已经明显上升，如果金融市场处于不稳定状态，美联储是否会选择此时加息，仍值得观察。他表示，如果美联储明天就开会，仅凭这份就业报告，他不会认为加息已成定局。 Orion首席投资官TIM HOLLAND也指出，强劲就业数据可能推动美债收益率走高，并给股市带来额外压力。当前市场本就受到AI资本开支周期前景和政策不确定性的影响，若利率进一步上升，风险资产可能继续承压。 Wealth Club首席投资策略师SUSANNAH STREETER则认为，强劲就业报告降低了近期降息的可能性，并强化了利率在更长时间内维持高位的判断。就业市场的韧性，也抵消了市场对数据中心建设放缓、AI监管增加可能拖累经济增长的部分担忧。 “新美联储通讯社”提出政策变量：美联储看滞后就业数据，还是前瞻性市场信号？ Nick Timiraos在社交媒体上指出，美国10月新增非农就业人数达到16.5万人，8月和9月数据合计上修8.4万人，失业率也小幅回落至约4.14%。无论采用何种观察口径，美国就业增长都在去年夏季接近停滞后重新加快。 但Timiraos认为，这些数据并不足以让美联储重新考虑其对经济增长和通胀的判断。真正值得关注的是，AI相关资产抛售是否会改变金融条件，进而影响美联储对政策效果的评估。 他提出的核心矛盾在于：美联储主席沃什曾表示，更愿意参考能够反映未来经济走势的市场信号，而不是滞后的经济数据。如今，就业报告显示经济增长仍具韧性，但AI相关资产抛售可能通过股价、融资条件和风险偏好影响金融环境。进入12月会议前，美联储究竟会更看重哪一类信号，可能成为政策讨论的关键。 这也意味着，尽管10月非农报告重新推高了加息预期，最终决策仍不只是就业数据的简单延伸。下一轮通胀数据将检验薪资和就业韧性是否转化为更持久的价格压力，而金融市场的变化则可能影响美联储对未来经济和政策传导的判断。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 美国11月密歇根消费者信心超预期升至三个月高位，独立选民信心提升，通胀预期改善
articles.summary: 受美国民众对个人财务及经济前景看法略有改善的提振，美国11月消费者信心指数升至三个月高位。 根据周五公布的调查，密歇根大学11月消费者信心指数初值从10月的48升至51。而彭博针对经济学家调查的预测中值为维持在48。 此番改善主要集中在独立选民群体中，他们报告的消费者信心创下一年来新高。相比之下，民主党和共和党选民的信心均有所恶化。 生活成本担忧仍是许多美国人最关心的问题。 约57%的受访者主动提到高物价侵蚀了他们的生活水平，这一比例创下自5月以来的新高。 尽管裁员有限且经济增长强劲，但随着物价涨幅快于工资增长，家庭财务状况依然紧绷。民主党在中期选举中的决定性胜利，反映出选民对经济现状的深刻不满，尤其是对食品、汽油和住房高昂成本的抱怨。 通胀预期改善，AI泡沫担忧浮现 未来一年的通胀预期有所改善，但仍处于高位。 消费者预计未来一年的物价将上涨4.3%，创三个月新低。他们还预计未来5至10年的物价年均涨幅为3.4%，较上月也有所回落。 调查负责人乔安妮·徐（Joanne Hsu）在一份声明中表示，除了对通胀的担忧外，“消费者的反馈还揭示了对可能出现的AI泡沫日益增长的焦虑。” 她补充道：“由于最近几周股市波动，持有大量股票投资组合的消费者个人财务状况本月下降了12%，降至自4月以来的最低水平，而其他所有财富群体的财务状况均有温和改善。” 11月衡量当前个人财务状况的指标升至四个高位，同时美国人对耐用品购买条件的看法也从历史低点回升。当前状况和预期状况指标均升至8月以来的最高水平。 本次调查期包含10月20日至11月2日的受访反馈。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 虚拟货币主要发行平台Solana高调“入沪”被紧急叫停！人民银行有关司局回应
articles.summary:
中国人民银行有关司局负责人介绍，近期监测发现，虚拟货币主要发行平台Solana通过境内相关单位高调投放广告，以推广Solana品牌的方式，进行虚拟货币营销宣传。中国人民银行联合相关地方金融管理、公安、市场监管等部门叫停线下交流活动，并将会同有关部门对涉事单位和个人开展调查。
该负责人进一步解释，Solana作为主要虚拟货币发行平台，其发行的Solana币本质上是虚拟货币，同时它也在为USDT等主要虚拟货币的发行交易提供技术服务，上述业务均属《通知》明确的非法金融活动，宣传推广Solana已违反《通知》规定。虚拟货币现阶段无法有效满足客户身份识别、反洗钱等方面的要求，易引发市场投机炒作活动。
该负责人表示，下一步，中国人民银行将与相关部门和地方政府一起，以境内虚拟货币交易商、境外虚拟货币发行交易平台的境内关联主体为重点，继续打击境内虚拟货币相关业务活动，维护好经济金融秩序。（金融时报） 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
